title: In Fellowship, Alone
description: In Fellowship, Alone in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 268.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: In fel-low-ship, a-lone, To God with faith draw near, Ap-proach his courts, be-siege his_ throne With all the powers of prayer: Go to his tem-ple, go, Nor from his al-tar move; Let ev-ery house his wor-ship know, And ev-ery heart his love.

lines: To God with faith draw near,
Approach his courts, besiege his throne
With all the powers of prayer:
Let every house his worship know,
Or groan, to him who reads the heart,
And now show forth his praise,
In shouts, or silent awe, adore
Pour out your souls to God,
And bow them with your knees,
And spread your hearts and hands abroad,
Extend the arms of mighty prayer,
From strength to strength go on,
Tread all the powers of darkness down,
Till Christ the Lord descend from high,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
